```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 6
)
library(cyclingpower)

results <- params$results
aligned <- results$aligned
settings <- results$settings
```

This compares `r dplyr::n_distinct(aligned$source)` power sources across
`r dplyr::n_distinct(aligned$run)` run(s).

Computed with a minimum power of `r settings$min_power` W, `r settings$width` W
bands showing only those with at least `r settings$min_seconds` seconds, clock
offsets sought up to `r settings$max_offset` s, and 95% intervals
from a moving-block bootstrap of `r settings$replicates` replicates over
`r settings$block`-second blocks
`r if (is.null(settings$seed)) "(unseeded, so the intervals move a little on a re-run)" else paste0("under seed ", settings$seed)`.

```{r files}
if (!is.null(results$spec)) {
  knitr::kable(results$spec, caption = "The files these results came from")
}
```

## Alignment

Two meters recording the same ride do not necessarily agree about what time it
is. Differencing on nominal timestamps when the clocks disagree compares power
from one moment against power from another, which inflates the spread and
shifts the average difference without any sign that anything went wrong. Each
source below was matched against a reference by cross-correlating the power
traces.

```{r alignment}
knitr::kable(results$alignment, digits = 3)
```

```{r alignment-note, results = "asis"}
unresolved <- results$alignment$source[results$alignment$status == "unresolved"]

if (length(unresolved) > 0) {
  cat(
    "> **Alignment incomplete.** No clock offset could be established for ",
    paste(unresolved, collapse = ", "),
    ", so the recorded timestamps stand. This is expected for a steady effort ",
    "with no features to lock onto; a low correlation instead suggests these ",
    "are not recordings of the same ride.\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

```{r timeseries}
plot_timeseries(aligned, smooth = settings$smooth)
```

## Overall agreement

`bias_w` is the average difference in watts and `gain_pc` the same thing as a
percentage, which is usually the more natural way to read a meter's error.
`loa_lower` and `loa_upper` bound the range within which most individual
seconds fall. Intervals come from a moving-block bootstrap rather than from
treating each second as independent evidence, which would make a fraction of a
watt look decisively different from zero.

```{r agreement}
knitr::kable(results$agreement, digits = 2)
```

```{r bland-altman}
plot_agreement(aligned, min_power = settings$min_power)
```

## Agreement across the power range

Meters often agree at endurance pace and diverge at threshold or in sprints,
which the single average above hides entirely.

The same bands are shown twice. In watts, a meter that is a constant
percentage out reads further from its partner the harder you ride, so the line
rises even though nothing about the meter changes; in per cent that same meter
is flat. A line that is level in watts and tilts in per cent, or tilts in both,
is a meter whose error genuinely depends on how hard you were riding.

```{r by-level-watts}
plot_by_level(results$by_level)
```

```{r by-level-percent}
plot_by_level(results$by_level, scale = "percent")
```

```{r by-level-alert, results = "asis"}
uneven <- level_dependence(results$by_level)
uneven <- uneven[uneven$separated, ]

for (i in seq_len(nrow(uneven))) {
  r <- uneven[i, ]
  cat(sprintf(
    paste(
      "> **%s and %s do not differ by a constant amount.** The gain runs from",
      "%+.1f%% at %s to %+.1f%% at %s in %s, and those two intervals do not",
      "overlap, so the overall average is not a good summary of this pair.\n\n"
    ),
    r$source_a, r$source_b, r$low_gain, r$low_band,
    r$high_gain, r$high_band, r$run
  ))
}
```

```{r by-level-table}
results$by_level |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Run = run,
    Pair = paste(source_a, "-", source_b),
    Band = band_range,
    Seconds = seconds,
    `Difference (W)` = sprintf("%+.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", bias_w, bias_lo, bias_hi),
    `Gain %` = sprintf("%+.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", gain_pc, gain_lo, gain_hi)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllrrr")
```

## Linking meters across runs

```{r chain, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(results$chained)) {
  cat(results$chain_error, "\n")
} else {
  cat("Bridge meter: **", results$chain$bridge, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(results$chain$assumption, "\n\n")
  cat(
    "The two runs overlap over ",
    round(100 * results$chain$overlap),
    "% of the power range they cover between them. Gains compared over ",
    "different parts of the range are not really comparable.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )
  print(knitr::kable(results$chained, digits = 2))
  cat("\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(results$chain$coverage, digits = 1))
}
```

```{r chain-plot}
if (!is.null(results$chained)) {
  plot_chain(results$chained)
}
```
